## Wanted 1: one day of Fleet Write by sender (2026-11-07, 2,283 strokes, all parsed)

- **2,283 strokes carried 3,042 actions, 1.33 per stroke. 1,870 strokes (81.9 %) carried exactly one action.** Size histogram: 1 → 1,870 · 2 → 214 · 3 → 172 · 4–9 → 16 · 10 → 11.
- Single-action strokes by op: `comment` 1,237 · `pr_create` 154 · `issue_patch` 146 · `issue_create` 101 · `labels_remove` 91 · `automerge_enable` 26 · `labels_add` 22 · `assign` 18 · other 75.
- Runner wall time: 18.8 h for the day (median run 32 s, p90 38 s). 2,278 succeeded and 5 failed.
- Targets: objectstack 1,968 · cloud 292 · docs.objectos.ai 17 · www.objectos.ai 3 · hotcrm 3.
- **A sender's next stroke lands a median ~45–55 s after its previous one**, which is about one relay round trip: the senders wait for each stroke to finish and then send the next one. In-session gaps: 1,098 of 2,157 are 60 s or less, and 1,537 are 180 s or less.

### What one stroke could have carried

A chain is a run of consecutive strokes from one session, each within the gap of the one before, capped at 20 actions. The saving is the number of strokes minus the number of chains.

| fold rule | runs saved | day after |
|---|---:|---:|
| same issue or PR, gap 180 s or less (no read-back dependency possible) | **471** | 1,812 (−21 %) |
| any target, gap 60 s or less, never after an op that creates the number (`issue_create`, `pr_create`, advisory create/report) | 1,017 | 1,266 (−45 %) |
| same rule, gap 180 s or less | 1,316 | 967 (−58 %) |

The second and third rows are upper bounds. A later stroke may still depend on reading the earlier one back. The first row is the floor that needs no new information.

Most common same-target chains (gap 180 s or less): `comment` → `labels_add+labels_remove+assign` 54 · `comment` → `labels_remove` 44 · `labels_add+labels_remove+assign` → `comment` 43 · `comment` → `comment` 25 · `labels_remove` → `comment` 19 · `issue_patch` → `comment` 17 · `labels_add+labels_remove` → `comment` 13 · `comment` → `labels_remove+unassign` 13. These are a claim or a release (labels + assignee, then the `Claim:`/`Release:` comment) sent as two strokes, because `post-stamped` and `label-write` each send their own stroke. Any-target pairs at 60 s or less: `comment` → `comment` on a different issue 238 (card note + mailbox or sibling card) · `comment` → `pr_ready+automerge_enable` 91 (verdict comment, then the landing).

## Wanted 2: the two `workflow_run` triggers

GitHub lets a `workflow_run` trigger filter on `workflows`, `types` and `branches`/`branches-ignore`. It cannot filter on the triggering run's event or conclusion. The [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow) say the branch filter names "what branches the triggering workflow must run on". Both files already narrow `types: [completed]`. Each job `if:` stays as it is and stays the authority.

| workflow | job `if:` filters on | head_branch of the runs it can act on | trigger narrowing | runs/day before → after (11-01..07 mean) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `merge-queue-triage.yml` | `event == 'merge_group'` and `conclusion == 'failure'` | `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-…` (read on 11-07: all 181 merge_group CI runs, and 0 runs of any other event on such a branch) | `branches: ['gh-readonly-queue/**']` | **757 → 263 (−65 %)**. Jobs that actually run (red merge_group CI) stay 125 for the week, about 18 a day. |
| `scheduled-full-run-card.yml` | `event == 'schedule'`, `head_branch == 'main'` and `conclusion` in (`failure`, `timed_out`) | `main` | `branches: [main]` | **1,512 → 269 (−82 %)**. That counts CI on `main` 939 + Lint on `main` 939 + UI Coverage 7 for the week, which is push + schedule. Filings unchanged. |

After the change, the triage and card runs that remain are the triggering runs whose event the trigger cannot see: `push` on `main` for the card, and green `merge_group` runs for triage. Those keep landing as skipped jobs, exactly as today. On 11-07 the three workflows together would have been 2,283 + 181 + 181 = 2,645 runs instead of 3,797.

Residual, stated rather than assumed: whether GitHub's branch matcher reads a `merge_group` run's `head_branch` the way the docs describe for other events is NOT MEASURED. A `workflow_run` workflow only runs from the default branch, so no PR can show it. The post-merge check is the next red merge_group CI run: it must produce a Merge Queue Triage run and its comment. Until one happens, the 7-day triage count is the reading.

Self-tests: neither the triage harness (`scripts/check-merge-queue-triage-outcome.mjs`, which reads the job's steps and permissions) nor the card's (`scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs`, which reads the `workflows:` line, the concurrency group and the crons) reads the trigger's branches. Both run on the change, and `branches:` goes on its own line so the `workflows:` regex is untouched.
